title: SLEEPING IN A UFO: The Isle of Wight's most extraordinary stay

content:
By CINDY-LOU DALE/ The modern traveller is no longer satisfied with simply booking a room. Increasingly, holidays are chosen not only for where they are, but for the stories they create. Whether spending the night in a converted lighthouse, a luxury treehouse or an underwater suite, experiential accommodation has become one of tourism’s fastest-growing sectors.

On England’s Isle of Wight, one campsite has embraced that trend with remarkable imagination.

Nestled beneath the ancient ramparts of Carisbrooke Castle, Windmill Campersite has transformed a former commercial North Sea oil-rig life raft into what may be Britain’s most unusual overnight stay – a fully illuminated UFO complete with an electric entrance hatch, glowing lights, smoke effects and an interior that looks as though it belongs in a Hollywood science-fiction film.

It is quirky. It is eccentric. It is unmistakably British. More importantly, it reflects a growing movement within the tourism industry, where memorable accommodation has become every bit as important as the destination itself.

From survival craft to spacecraft

Long before welcoming holidaymakers, the vessel had a very different purpose. Built as a self-contained emergency life raft for workers stationed on commercial oil platforms in the middle of the Atlantic Ocean, its original role was to preserve life in some of the world’s harshest maritime conditions.

Today it has been given a second life altogether. The circular capsule now resembles a landed alien spacecraft. Guests enter through a fully electric opening door before stepping into a surprisingly comfortable interior complete with atmospheric lighting, leather seating, a smoke machine, toilet facilities and a distinctive crescent-shaped bed.

Outside, the illusion continues. The UFO sits inside its own “docking station,” itself ingeniously converted from a former supermarket refrigerated delivery lorry.

Where frozen groceries were once transported around Britain, visitors now find two bunk beds sleeping up to four guests, a fully equipped kitchen and comfortable living facilities.

It is a wonderful example of creative recycling meeting imaginative tourism.

One extraordinary stay among many

Remarkably, the UFO is only one of Windmill Campersite’s collection of unusual accommodation. Owner Stewart Dungey has spent almost a decade transforming his working farm into one of Britain’s most inventive glamping destinations.

The journey began in 2016 after spotting a former Falklands rescue helicopter advertised on eBay. Rather than seeing redundant military equipment, Dungey saw holiday accommodation. The helicopter became the site’s first headline attraction, soon joined by an extraordinary collection of equally imaginative conversions.

Guests can spend the night inside a replica submarine inspired by a James Bond film, relax in traditional shepherd’s huts, stay in a charming dairy cottage or embrace colourful nostalgia in a Bollywood-themed split-screen Volkswagen camper.

Every accommodation tells its own story and together they create a destination unlike anywhere else in Britain.

More than somewhere to sleep

The creativity extends far beyond the accommodation itself. Communal facilities have been designed with equal imagination. An old agricultural silo has become a private cinema. A converted Robin Reliant now houses the campsite’s laundrette.

Families gather around a large communal firepit to toast marshmallows beneath the stars, while pizza ovens, barbecue facilities and outdoor dining encourage guests to linger long into warm summer evenings. There is even a silent disco housed within its own quirky structure.

These shared spaces transform the campsite into a genuine community where children quickly make friends and adults rediscover the simple pleasures of outdoor living.

Discovering the Isle of Wight

While the accommodation provides plenty of reasons to stay put, Windmill Campersite also occupies an ideal position for exploring one of England’s most charming islands.

Carisbrooke Castle, standing proudly above the campsite, has watched over the island for nearly a thousand years. Its medieval walls, Norman keep and famous donkeys that once powered the castle’s well continue to delight visitors of all ages.

Elsewhere, the Isle of Wight offers more than 800 km of footpaths and cycle trails weaving through rolling countryside, dramatic chalk cliffs and picturesque villages.

The iconic Needles, rising dramatically from the sea at the island’s western tip, remain among England’s most recognizable coastal landmarks.

Golden beaches stretch along much of the coastline, while seaside towns such as Shanklin, Ventnor and Cowes offer everything from traditional fish and chips to independent boutiques and excellent seafood restaurants.

For families, fossil hunting along the island’s beaches has become something of a rite of passage, with dinosaur footprints and prehistoric discoveries continuing to reinforce the Isle of Wight’s reputation as Britain’s Dinosaur Island.

Easy to reach

Despite feeling wonderfully removed from mainland Britain, the Isle of Wight is surprisingly accessible. Regular ferry services connect Portsmouth and Lymington with the island, while hovercraft services provide one of the fastest crossings from Southsea to Ryde.

Guests staying at Windmill Campersite also benefit from a 25% discount on selected Wightlink vehicle ferry crossings, making the journey even more appealing for families travelling by car.

Within an hour of leaving the mainland, visitors find themselves entering an altogether different world.

The appeal of experiential travel

Accommodation has become one of the defining elements of modern tourism. Travellers increasingly want stories they can share as much as destinations they can visit.

Windmill Campersite understands that perfectly. Sleeping inside a former oil-rig life raft disguised as a UFO is not simply somewhere to spend the night. It becomes the holiday itself.

Combined with imaginative communal facilities, outstanding countryside and the timeless appeal of the Isle of Wight, the campsite offers an experience that appeals to families, couples, glamping enthusiasts and travellers searching for something delightfully unexpected.

Sometimes the most memorable holidays begin not with the destination, but with where you choose to sleep.

Travel trade insight

Windmill Campersite reflects one of the strongest trends shaping tourism: experience-led accommodation. Unique stays consistently generate strong social media engagement and appeal to families, multi-generational groups, couples and travellers looking for something genuinely different. Its location beneath Carisbrooke Castle, combined with discounted Wightlink ferry crossings, makes it an attractive product for UK self-drive holidays.

For travel advisors and tour operators, experiential travel and family holidays, Windmill Campersite offers a highly marketable product that combines novelty with broad destination appeal.

Getting there

The Isle of Wight is reached by regular ferry services from Portsmouth, Southampton and Lymington, together with hovercraft services between Southsea and Ryde. Windmill Campersite is located close to Carisbrooke Castle, approximately 10 minutes by road from the ferry terminal at East Cowes. Guests booking accommodation receive a 25% discount on selected Wightlink vehicle ferry crossings, adding further value for self-drive visitors.
